summary: Feed s173_triple is degraded: NDR port overloaded by 12.94 Gbps microbursts (129% of 10G), 11% duplicates, and 93.3% encrypted traffic exceeds 90% tolerance. No packet drops, one-way, or VLAN issues detected.

findings.root_cause: Peak 12.94 Gbps in 1 ms burst vs 10 Gbps NDR port (129% capacity, 2 overloaded intervals). Caused by aggregated SPAN/TAP feeds microbursting without shaping or load balancing to the tool port.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR ingress buffers overrun and drops packets at line rate, causing incomplete flows, broken session reassembly, and missed detections.

recommended_fix.why: Spread bursty traffic across 2+ 10G tool ports via packet broker load balancing to keep per-port utilization below 80% and prevent burst drops

findings.root_cause: 11.0% duplicates (876 of 7992 packets, threshold 5%) indicates overlapping SPAN sessions or duplicate TAP feeds aggregated on the packet broker without deduplication.
findings.impact_on_tool: Wastes NDR processing and storage, inflates flow counts and alerts, skews analytics and can cause false positives while reducing effective detection capacity.

recommended_fix.why: Enable broker-level deduplication to remove identical packets within a short window before delivery, restoring correct traffic counts

findings.root_cause: 93.3% of bytes are encrypted vs NDR tolerance of 90%, meaning almost all payload is TLS/encrypted and delivered opaque to the NDR which needs full payload.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR is blind to payload content and limited to metadata/flow analysis, significantly reducing detection coverage for threats inside encrypted sessions.

recommended_fix.why: Decrypt relevant TLS via visibility fabric or provide session keys to NDR to restore payload inspection while respecting privacy/compliance policy
